html:
The Ottoman sultan who took Constantinople in 1453, aged 21, and made it the capital of his empire. He is known in Turkish as Fatih, the Conqueror.

Son of Murad II, he ruled briefly as a boy and then from 1451 to 1481. He prepared the siege carefully. He built Rumelihisarı to close the Bosporus, hired Orban to cast giant cannon, and had ships dragged overland into the Golden Horn. The city fell on 29 May 1453.

He then rebuilt and repopulated it, turned Hagia Sophia into a mosque, began Topkapı Palace and the Grand Bazaar, and made Gennadius Scholarius patriarch of the Orthodox. His armies took Serbia, the Morea, Trebizond, Bosnia and much more, and landed at Otranto in Italy in 1480.

He was curious about the West, read Greek and Italian books, and had the Venetian painter Gentile Bellini paint his portrait. Under him the Ottoman Empire became a world power.
